title: Task-report scope splits by drive-letter casing on Windows: hook and MCP server disagree, hunch_task returns task not found
observation: Observed 2026-09-14 in the hunch repo on Windows 11. scopeOf(root) in src/core/taskReport.ts and promptTaskId/nativeHookCwd in src/core/taskReportHook.ts hash fs.realpathSync(root), which on Windows preserves the caller's drive-letter casing (c:\Users\... vs C:\Users\...), while realpathSync.native returns canonical on-disk casing. Claude Code spawned the prompt hook with cwd C:\... and the MCP server with c:\..., so the hook opened tasks under scope sha256:f0d5ed33... and the MCP server looked them up under sha256:f9e54103...: 8 tasks under one scope, 6 under the other in .hunch-cache/served.db. Passing cwd: C:\... to hunch_task does not help because the MCP re-root check compares canonicalRootPath (native) and concludes the roots are equal, so root keeps its original casing and no re-home happens. Result: hunch_task start/finish failed with 'task not found in this repository/worktree' for 3 of 4 prompts in one session, no contribution card, and hunch task list / VS Code Contribution view / hunch task status (promptTaskId) each see only half the ledger. Other non-native realpath scope sites: src/taskReports.ts:23 (createTaskReporter), src/core/taskReportEvidence.ts:38. Fix direction: one canonical scope path (realpathSync.native with realpathSync fallback) shared by hook, MCP, CLI and reporter; readTask may additionally accept the legacy non-native hash so tasks open during upgrade survive. Secondary, dev-checkout only: hooks registered twice (.claude/settings.json runs npx tsx src; .claude/settings.local.json runs stale dist built 08:39 titled 'Claude task'), so every prompt receives two UserPromptSubmit blocks and the src hook falls into its legacy-title branch.
evidence: .hunch-cache/served.db report_tasks grouped by scope (2026-09-14): f0d5ed33 count 8, f9e54103 count 6, same repository
